messages:
maria: heads-up — canary 2026.3.8 rolled last night started OOMs on several longctx hosts (12/48). CI perf job flagged p99 token throughput regressed ~11%. deploy-bot: rollout automatically halted for canary cluster :warning:

alex: reproed locally on a 32GB GPU instance, memory climbs steadily with mixed sequence lengths. saw KV slab fragmentation spike in the profiler around 200s into workload.

ji-hoon: bisect started. quick summary: two suspicious CLs landed in the same window — runtime:adaptive-evict-score (c3f2b9) and kernel-router:prefer-shortseq-fast-kernel (a9d1f4). both touched alloc/evict heuristics.

sam: good call. CI perf history shows the delta aligns with that merge window. the perf check: `ci/perf` shows -11% p99 throughput and +9% mem churn on longctx tests.

alex: here's the quick heap diff from pprof after 5 minutes (shortened):
```
# before: slab_total=12.4GB, slab_free=3.2GB, slab_frag=1.1GB
# after:  slab_total=13.1GB, slab_free=1.0GB, slab_frag=2.7GB
# metadata objects ~37% increase
```

maria: interestingly, the kernel-router change prefers the "fast" kernel for short sequences which reduces batching. that reduces average batch size by ~18% in our trace — so eviction runs more often on smaller batches and creates many tiny hot slab allocations.

ji-hoon: reproducer attached (small script) — run with mixed seq lengths and enable verbose allocator logs: `./test/mix_seq_repro --len-dist=short:0.6,long:0.4 --alloc-log=1` gave repeated small slab allocations and evict thrash.

sam: tried reverting adaptive-evict-score locally and left kernel-router as-is: memory improved but not back to baseline. then reverted kernel-router too -> memory returns close to baseline and CI perf flip goes away. so seems both interact.

maria: rollback plan? we should revert both CLs on canary and hold until we have a fix that accounts for batch-size change in the evict scoring. recommend partial revert: revert adaptive-evict-score first (it touches eviction math) and pause kernel-router rollout. open to revert both if canary still bad.

alex: opened a revert PR for runtime: https://repo/infra/runtime/pulls/842 (revert c3f2b9). deploy-bot: revert PR merged, canary redeploy started.

deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered by manual revert — rollout at 10% -> 100% over 8m.

ji-hoon: after revert -> rerun perf harness: p99 throughput delta to baseline is now +1% (noise) and slab_frag dropped back to ~1.2GB. heap growth stopped on longctx traces.

maria: next steps: 1) re-opened a follow-up issue to make evict score aware of observed batch-size distribution (evict_score := f(size, seq_len_hist, recent_batch_count)). 2) add synthetic CI test that simulates mixed-length traces with kernel-router config matrix so we catch interactions. 3) put kernel-router rollout on hold until scoring is adjusted and we have a canary pass.

sam: adding CI matrix test now. quick config diff that caused issue for reference:
```
# kernel-router patch (a9d1f4)
- prefer_kernel = "balanced"
+ prefer_kernel = "fast_shortseq"

# runtime evict (c3f2b9)
- evict_score = base + age*0.4
+ evict_score = base + age*0.6 - batch_factor*0.1
```

maria: thanks all. filing an incident note and tagging eng-sre so we can correlate infra-level metrics. marking this thread for the release postmortem. :white_check_mark:
